# Sirach Chapter 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_002_page_001.jpg

---

**2:1** My child, if you come forward to serve the Lord, prepare your soul for testing.

**2:2** Set your heart right and be steadfast, and do not be in a hurry in time of disaster.

**2:3** Cling to him and do not depart, so that you may be honored at the end of your days.

**2:4** Accept whatever is brought upon you, and in changes that humble you be patient.

**2:5** For gold is tested in fire, and those acceptable to God in the furnace of humiliation.

**2:6** Trust in him and he will help you; make your ways straight and hope in him.

**2:7** You who fear the Lord, wait for his mercy, and do not turn aside lest you fall.

**2:8** You who fear the Lord, trust in him, and your reward will not be lost.

**2:9** You who fear the Lord, hope for good things, for everlasting joy and mercy.

**2:10** Consider the ancient generations and see: who trusted in the Lord and was put to shame? Or who remained in the fear of him and was forsaken? Or who called upon him and was overlooked?

**2:11** For the Lord is compassionate and merciful; he forgives sins and saves in time of affliction.

**2:12** Woe to timid hearts and slack hands, and to the sinner who walks a double path.

**2:13** Woe to the faint heart, for it does not trust! Therefore it will not be sheltered.

**2:14** Woe to you who have lost your endurance! What will you do when the Lord visits you?

**2:15** Those who fear the Lord do not disobey his words, and those who love him keep his ways.

**2:16** Those who fear the Lord seek to please him, and those who love him are filled with his law.

**2:17** Those who fear the Lord prepare their hearts, and humble their souls before him.

**2:18** Let us fall into the hands of the Lord, and not into the hands of men; for as his majesty is, so also is his mercy.

---

*Translator's Note: The chapter contains a structured series of three groups: those commanded to prepare (vv.1-6), those addressed with "you who fear the Lord" (vv.7-11), and contrasts between the faithful and the faint-hearted (vv.12-18). Greek anastrepho in v.3 = "do not depart/turn away."*
